summary: This benchmark evaluates an adaptive witness routing policy for 3D write gates under rotating fault conditions on a 64³ voxel grid. The adaptive policy achieves a 17.71 percentage point gain in post-rotation word recovery over calibration-only baselines and matches an orientation oracle. The paper provides rigorous statistical reporting and environment details, though it is tested only on synthetic axis-aligned faults and lacks broader architectural context.
strengths: Methodology is mathematically well-defined, isolating directional co-activation via an exponential moving average update rule without requiring ground-truth fault labels.
Benchmark includes both blind baselines (fixed axis, calibrate once) and an informative upper-bound comparator (fixed perpendicular given true orientation).
Presents paired statistical analysis with 95% bootstrap confidence intervals for recovery rate deltas across 12 independent world generations.
Provides complete environment specifications including hardware configuration, peak MLX memory footprint, exact runtime, and library versions.
weaknesses: The evaluation is restricted to idealized synthetic scenarios with axis-aligned, globally uniform fault rotations on a periodic 64³ grid.
The article lacks foundational context explaining the high-level computing substrate, physical or virtual write model, and rationale for categorization under 'ai/fine-tuning'.
No supporting repository was submitted directly to the Pubroot harness, limiting independent verification to external links under a 'text_only' badge.
suggestions: Recategorize the paper under an architecture or fault-tolerant computing category rather than 'ai/fine-tuning' unless explicit fine-tuning connections are detailed.
Expand the scope of the benchmark to non-axis-aligned, spatially heterogeneous, and localized fault distributions.
Provide a brief conceptual introduction defining the write gate mechanism, detector training, and practical target applications.

claims.text: On a 262,144-voxel grid, the controller recovered 70.38% of stored 32-bit words after a fault rotation by routing to a different witness. Keeping the direction chosen during calibration recovered 52.67%.
claims.source: Internal experimental reporting and arithmetic verification on 64x64x64 periodic grid dimensions (64³ = 262,144 voxels)

claims.text: On rotated faults the adaptive policy gained 17.71 percentage points over the calibration-only policy, with a paired 95% interval of 8.97 to 26.55 points.
claims.source: Submission data table difference calculation (70.38% - 52.67% = 17.71 pp) and paired statistical reporting

claims.text: It used an Apple M5 Ultra with 80 GPU cores, 256 GiB memory, macOS 27.2, Python 3.12.16, MLX 0.32.4 and NumPy 2.5.5.
claims.source: Apple hardware and software release specifications for M5 Ultra Mac Studio (80-core GPU, 256GB unified memory) and macOS 27 Golden Gate
